bull_case: 유리한 사업·자본배분 가정이 유지되면 기준 점수보다 높은 결과가 가능하다.
bear_case: 성장·마진·자본배분이 정상화되고 핵심 불확실성이 불리하게 전개되면 기준 점수보다 낮아질 수 있다.
thesis: Berkshire's structural advantage is a portfolio of durable, independently cash-generative businesses plus permanent capital and insurance float. It is resilient rather than hyper-growth.

evidence.claim: Operating earnings in H1 2026 came from underwriting, insurance investment income, BNSF, BHE and manufacturing/service/retail.
H1 BNSF earnings were $2.935B and BHE earnings $2.005B.

counterevidence: Insurance investment income falls as rates normalize.
Rail, housing and industrial assets remain cyclical.
Scale makes future capital allocation progressively harder.
unknowns: Long-run economics of Taylor Morrison after integration.
Incremental regulated returns at BHE under rising capital needs.
falsifiers: Two or more major earnings engines enter structural decline simultaneously.
Insurance float shrinks persistently and becomes costly.
Capital allocation fails to offset mature-subsidiary stagnation.

subscores.rationale: Insurance, freight rail, regulated energy/utilities and industrial businesses have durable multi-decade demand.
Several subsidiaries are leaders, while the parent advantage is capital allocation rather than a single category standard.
Independent earnings engines span insurance, rail, energy and manufacturing/service/retail, reducing single-cycle dependence.
